one_month_reasoning: Three events fall in the window. Q3 2026 results come before the open on 2026-10-28 (guide $9.3-9.4B and $0.70-0.71 EPS) [1,2,4]. Hyperscaler Q3 prints and 2027 capex commentary land in the last week of October, and TE's FQ4 is expected Oct 28 - Nov 2 [28]. The latest channel checks are constructive: connector book-to-bill is 1.2-1.3x, bookings are accelerating out of the summer, lead times are extending, and CY27 planning points to double-digit growth [23]. So a beat is likely. But the verified reaction history (+3.6%, -12.2% on a beat in Jan, +3.2%, +4.5%) [29] says a beat does not guarantee a gain, and the downside is larger when the guide disappoints. I model 85% of the mass as lognormal with median $86.8 and sigma 12%, and 15% as a 'sell the news / weak guide' component with median $80 and sigma 15%. Overall median is about $86.0, essentially flat, with a modest left skew. The spread is near annual vol/3.5. P(>=85.67) is 0.51.

fair_value.method: Weighted 60/40: forward P/E (2028E EPS $3.72 x 24x = $89.3) and forward EV/EBITDA (2028E EBITDA $14.3B x 17x, less ~$10B net debt, over 2.578B shares = $90.7). The blend is $90, the value on 2027-10-01 priced on the next 12 months' earnings. It is down from $93 because I cut 2028 growth to 13% / 12%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Oakridge's 25.2x forward P/E at $82.57 implies $3.28 [15]. The supervisor cross-check across agents gave $3.28-3.29. The Q3 guide of $0.705/qtr [2] annualized and grown ~17% gives about $3.3.

Cut from 17%. Hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply in 2028: Goldman +12% [27], UBS +6% [26]. Dell'Oro's path from ~$1T in 2026 to $1.7T in 2030 implies about 14%/yr [25]. Channel checks still point to double-digit CY27 growth and new TPU content [23]. Kyber share dilution [21] mostly affects 2H27-28 NVDA volume. Net: revenue growth around 11-12% plus a little operating leverage gives 13%.
Today's forward P/E is 25.2x [15]. I take off about 1x as growth slows from 50%+ to the low teens. Bernstein's $99 target [20] and GF Value of $80.73 [19] bracket the result.

bear.story: AI capex digestion arrives in 2027 as 2028 budgets flatten (UBS +6%). Kyber goes multi-source with Foxconn Interconnect as the major midplane supplier, so APH's Nvidia rack content shrinks for Rubin Ultra. IT datacom book-to-bill drops below 1. 2028E EPS stalls around $3.1, and the multiple falls to about 18.5x.

base.story: 2027 capex lands at about $1.0-1.2T and grows low double digits into 2028. APH licenses its VR Ultra backplane IP and keeps a meaningful share of Kyber, while gaining TPU9i cabled-backplane content (>$750/TPU) and CommScope fiber. 2028E EPS is about $3.72 at roughly 24.5x.

bull.story: Capex surprises toward Goldman's $1.2T and $1.4T path. TPU and custom-ASIC backplanes plus 1.6T ramps more than offset Kyber dilution, and connector shortages support pricing. NTM EPS reaches about $4.25 and the multiple holds near 29x.

thesis_break_reason: $58 sits below the 2026 closing floor ($59.58 on Mar 30, $59.60 on May 19) and the 52-week intraday low of $59.01. It is about 17.6x 2027E EPS. A close there would most likely mean estimates are being cut (datacom book-to-bill below 1, hyperscaler 2027 budgets cut, or confirmed large Kyber and TPU share losses), not a routine AI-rotation de-rating like May's, which held at $59.6. I keep $58 rather than the supervisor's $60 because a test of the $59-60 floor itself has happened twice on rotation alone.

reasoning: Round 2. I accepted two supervisor findings. (1) Every capex forecaster has 2028 growth slowing hard (Goldman +12%, UBS +6%) [26,27], and Dell'Oro's ~$1T (2026) to $1.7T (2030) path implies about 14%/yr [25]. So I cut 2028 EPS growth from 17% to 13% and EBITDA growth from 15% to 12%. Fair value falls from $93 to $90. (2) I dropped the 'APH supplies the Kyber midplane' positive, which rested on a 2025 X post and secondary blogs. GF Securities reports that Foxconn Interconnect may be the major Kyber midplane supplier [21,22]. I verified the report's existence but not its date, and APH reportedly fell 5% on it [22]. I partly disagree on the size of the hit. A newer Edgewater channel check (2026-09-30) says APH is expected to license its VR Ultra backplane IP to FIT and TE at Nvidia's request [23]. That reads as share dilution on an APH-designed part, not outright loss. Kyber ships only in 2H27 [24], so the impact by Oct 2027 is mostly sentiment and 2028 estimates. The same check has APH as lead designer of the TPU9i cabled backplane (connector TAM >$750/TPU vs $300-350), CommScope fiber lead times stretching to ~50 weeks, connector book-to-bill at 1.2-1.3x and CY27 double-digit planning [23]. Those are offsets. Net: a slightly bigger, slightly fatter bear case (0.24 at $57), and a lower base ($91) and bull ($122). The 12-month distribution is a mixture: 76% lognormal with median $93.5 and sigma 0.30, plus 24% lognormal with median $61 and sigma 0.36. That gives a median of about $86, a mean of about $90 (equal to fair value) and P(>=86) of 0.50. The 1-month ladder stays near flat with a small left skew, per the verified earnings-reaction history [29]. Research was limited: Intellectia and MSN pages did not render, so the GF report's details come from search snippets.
